Inside a container, `localhost:8002` points to the container itself unless the mock backend is run as a second service. The backend repository is `https://github.com/ECCdigital/smart-city-booking-backend` — the README states it may be self-hosted. The mock backend might be part of that repo. So the mock backend must be reachable at localhost:8002 from inside the container. This requires host networking, or running the mock inside the same container network with that name, or running the mock as a sidecar container on shared-net and aliasing it as "localhost"... no, that won't work.

If I add an environment variable like `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, or install the certificate into the container's trust store... but the certificate is self-signed for their domain — I can fetch it with curl -k, extract the public certificate, and install it into the container's trust store. That might actually work: curl -k https://your_tenant-api.smart-city-booking.de/auth/... let me probe the endpoints.
